sections.content:
SPACE did something interesting! The white block (id=13) changed from white (W) to purple (p), and the HUD bar (id=14) changed from dark gray (c) to white (W). Looking at the image, the bottom block now has two parts - purple on top and white on bottom. It seems like SPACE swaps or changes the color of the block below the gray-bordered room.
Let me understand the pattern:
- The top-left panel shows a white block above a purple block (reference pattern)
- The center has a purple block in a gray border, with a white block below it
- SPACE seems to have changed the white block to purple (top half) and added white below
Wait, looking more carefully at the segmentation:
- id=13 was W (white), 100 pixels, boundary [[34, 27], [34, 36], [43, 36], [43, 27]] - a 10x10 white square
- After SPACE: id=13 is p (purple), 50 pixels, boundary [[34, 27], [34, 36], [38, 36], [38, 27]] - a 5x10 purple rectangle (top half)
- id=14 is W (white), 50 pixels, boundary [[39, 27], [39, 36], [43, 36], [43, 27]] - a 5x10 white rectangle (bottom half)
So SPACE split the white block into two halves: purple on top, white on bottom. This matches the pattern shown in the top-left panel (white on top, purple on bottom... wait, no).
Actually, looking at the top-left panel:
- id=5: W (white), 50 pixels, boundary [[3, 3], [3, 12], [7, 12], [7, 3]] - white block on top
- id=9: p (purple), 50 pixels, boundary [[8, 3], [8, 12], [12, 12], [12, 3]] - purple block below
So the reference pattern is white on top, purple on bottom. After SPACE, the bottom block became purple on top (id=13) and white on bottom (id=14) - which is the REVERSE of the reference pattern.
Hmm, let me look at the current image again - it shows the purple block in the gray border, then below it a purple block, then a white block. So SPACE created a purple+white stack below the gray-bordered room.
The goal might be to match the top-left pattern (white above purple). Let me try SPACE again to see if it cycles through states.
